revision: rev01 pass 2 (revision brief: FEEDBACK.md). Proposals from FEEDBACK.md are the working defaults here: 7 bank poses on 31x33 with pivot (15,16); pose transitions of 40-65 ms; plasma charges while fire is held, about 0.9 s to full, releasing early fires nothing; nova 12 frames / 620 ms; 17 plasma effect frames; 7 flash counterparts; the proposed projectile sizes. Each is marked "proposal" where it appears. Gate 1 (owner, 24 Oct 2026): studies approved as stills; player candidate N1, round hostile orb, needle pre-baked at 0/22.5/45 degrees, nova stored as a sparse tile atlas by the consumer.

conventions.units: pixels in the 640x360 logical view; 1 texel = 1 logical pixel, no runtime scaling
conventions.origin: top-left of each canvas, +x right, +y down
conventions.pivot: canvas pixel the game position maps to; sockets are offsets from the pivot, +y down
conventions.canvas: odd width and odd height, so a symmetric ship has a 1 px centre column and the pivot sits on a whole pixel (also after the engine's -90 degree rotation of the Kiln parts); backgrounds are exempt
conventions.alpha: binary: palette index 0 is transparent, every other pixel fully opaque
conventions.frames: one full palette-index grid per frame (baked frames), stored as a horizontal strip PNG, frames left to right in 'frames' order; a sprite with 'canvases' lists one canvas per frame instead of one shared 'canvas'
conventions.sockets: a socket is [dx, dy] from the pivot, a list of them, or an object keyed by frame name when it moves per pose; a per-pose socket must be given for every frame
conventions.bounds: 'damage' is the collision shape the game may use (circle radius from the pivot, or a rect [w, h] centred on it); 'glow' is the decorative extent that promises no damage
conventions.muzzles: a muzzle socket is the first transparent pixel straight ahead of the muzzle centre (the pixel a shot is spawned on); exhaust sockets are the centre of the nozzle exit on the row below it
conventions.edges: no opaque pixel on a canvas edge row or column, except where the canvas is exactly the sprite's shape (primaryLance 3x11, hostileNeedle head columns)

viewport.presentation: integer scale k = floor(min(screenW / 640, screenH / 360)) in device pixels; the remainder is letterbox/pillarbox in the clear colour
viewport.smallWindowPolicy: if the formula gives k = 0 (viewport smaller than 640x360 device pixels) use k = 1, centre the 640x360 canvas and let the viewport clip it equally on both sides; never scale by a fraction, so the pixel grid stays whole. Such windows are not a supported play target.

optionalTallMode.use: 16:10 screens only; the extra 40 rows hold background and HUD, never playfield

palette.note: One shared indexed palette. Ramps are contiguous and ordered dark -> light. Index 0 is transparent. Indices 1-55 are the original hull and environment ramps and are never recoloured; 56-76 are effect ramps added for the projectile, plasma and nova vocabulary.

palette.backgrounds: each stage background has its own palette of at most 32 colours; it must not use any colour of the fire, glow, pickup or cockpit ramps, nor of the effect ramps (plasma, bead, needle, orb, nova), and its lightest value (Rec. 709 luma) stays below the steel ramp's lightest (216.0)

animation.note: proposal: adjacent pose levels are traversed in 40-65 ms while input changes; poses are input states, not a loop; the return to neutral is immediate. Final thresholds need playback.

sprites.design: compact armed spacecraft: armoured prow, recessed cockpit, substantial engine pods, visible weapon housings, negative spaces between hull sections; blue/cyan identity with a small warm cockpit accent. Banks are whole-body rolls (raised pod shows its top, lowered pod its side/underside, canopy displaces, hull overlaps, extreme silhouette narrows), re-lit per pose. The pivot (gameplay core) stays fixed.
sprites.socketStatus: measured from the finished 7-pose art by source/player.py (Phase 2); playerFlash shares them

sprites.role: damage flash: one high-value counterpart per bank pose, same silhouette and sockets as player; shown for one brief flash when hit, then the invulnerability cue takes over
sprites.cuePriority: proposal: damage flash first (overrides everything for its duration), then the invulnerability bright/dim alternation (runtime opacity, the core marker stays visible), while the charge-ready cue stays visible at the plasma muzzle throughout; the low-hull cue is persistent and separate from the temporary damage state
sprites.socketStatus: identical to player, pose by pose (same silhouettes)

sprites.role: player primary fire: narrow cyan/white lance, pointed head at the top, short fading tail; may be rendered by code from this sprite's colours
ordinary hostile fire: round coral/pink bead with a dark separation rim
aimed fast hostile fire: red/orange needle or arrowhead, drawn pointing down (+y) and rotated by the renderer toward its velocity
sprites.directions: frames point down (+y) rotated 0, 22.5 and 45 degrees clockwise on screen (tip swings from straight down toward -x). The 16 directions are angle = k*90 + {0, 22.5, 45, 67.5} degrees: frames needle-0, needle-22, needle-45 and needle-22 mirrored across the down-left diagonal (PIL TRANSVERSE), each then turned k quarter turns clockwise. Colours are symmetric, so mirroring flips no lighting. Centre of mass of every frame is on the pivot.

radii.note: proposal: outer ring radius per frame, px from the origin. Canvas = 2R+3 for ignite/expand frames (1 px margin) and 2(R+12)+1 for fade frames (embers drift up to 10 px outward). Band width: 4 px at r10, 5 at r40, 8 at r110, 9 from r200 on, as 1 px white front + 1-2 yellow + gold body + 1-2 orange, with inner tabs up to 3 px (study C)
radii.derivation: farthest visible corner from any legal player position: player clamp [24..616]x[57..319] in the 640x360 view (the 480x270 clamp scaled by 4/3); the worst case is a low origin to a top corner, (24,319) to (640,0) = 693.7 px, so fade-2 (r695) is the corner-reach frame
radii.staging: re-staged after Phase 2 build 1: from the screen centre the farthest visible point is ~406 px, so the coherent ring now ends at r410 (expand-5) and thinning starts on screen; the corner reach (690) falls on fade-2, so fade-2 keeps ~40% of the circumference with its front intact on the kept arcs. Trade-off recorded for gate 2: from a central origin the farthest visible point is ~406-452 px, so the fade frames (r500+) are seen only when the player is near an edge or corner; thinning from r300-400 would show dissipation in normal play but weaken the corner reach

sprites.origin: fixed at the player position when the nova is triggered; the ring does not follow the ship

animation.note: proposal from FEEDBACK.md priority 3; the bullet-clear/damage event fires on trigger, not after the ignition frames

sprites.layering: above hulls, smoke and the explosion; below hostile bullet cores, the beam lane and the HUD; interior stays transparent
sprites.reducedMotion: a quieter alternative with an equally clear activation cue is delivered with the frames (Phase 2)
sprites.storage: gate 1 decision: delivered as full frames in the strip; the consumer packs them into a sparse 32x32 tile atlas (only non-empty tiles, with offsets), about 1.7 M texels
sprites.fade: fade-0 (r500) keeps ~75% of the circumference with chunks up to 5-6 px under an intact white front; fade-1 (r590) ~55%, chunks up to 4 px; fade-2 (r690) ~40%, chunks up to 3 px, front intact on kept arcs; fade-3 (r760) ~20%, mostly embers

sprites.role: reduced-motion / low-flash nova: ignite-1 of the nova strip is held about 120 ms at the ship as a local flare, then one thin static ring at r=110 (1 px white front + 1 px gold) is shown, swapped once for its broken version; cleared bullets become in-place ember clusters (consumer)

codeDrawn.note: Code rendering stays allowed. Projectiles now have authored sprites above (primaryLance, hostileBead, hostileNeedle, hostileOrb, plasmaShot); the renderer may draw them from those sprites or reproduce them with rects using the same ramp colours, as long as shape and size match. Shape is assigned to behaviour consistently (one shape per weapon role), never picked per shot. Dangerous cores sit above hulls, smoke and debris; trails are subordinate to the core.
